source-integrity.freshness: Q2 FY2027 primary results dated 2026-08-26 plus market valuation observed 2026-09-25
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: issuer Q2 release and SEC filing are not counted as independent corroboration when describing the same reported facts
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: current valuation cross-checked with independent market-data source; issuer claims remain issuer-origin evidence

company-underwriting.operatingFinancialTrajectory: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $805m, up 11% YoY; subscription revenue rose 12%; RPO rose 17% and cRPO 14%. GAAP operating margin improved to 13% from 6%, operating cash flow was $234m and free cash flow $227m.
company-underwriting.contractsBacklogCustomersSuppliers: RPO of $4.858b and cRPO of $2.585b support forward contracted demand. Identity is software-based with limited physical supply-chain exposure, while customer trust and cloud/platform dependencies remain material operational dependencies.
company-underwriting.balanceSheetRunwayDebtDilution: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $2.299b at July 31, 2026; the remaining $350m 2026 Notes principal was settled in cash. Current market data shows approximately $34.13b market cap and $31.88b enterprise value.
company-underwriting.managementGovernanceCapitalAllocation: Founder-led CEO continuity and improving profitability support execution credibility; historical security incidents and the need to maintain identity-platform trust prevent exceptional governance treatment.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: High subscription mix and expanding GAAP/FCF margins support moderate pricing/value capture, but Microsoft and broader suite bundling constrain structural pricing power.
catalysts: Q3 FY2027 execution against $813m-$817m revenue guidance

thesisQuality.basis: Identity is a durable security control plane with $4.858b RPO and expanding products, but vendor-specific moat is moderated by suite competition and trust sensitivity.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue grew 11%, cRPO 14%, GAAP operating margin reached 13% versus 6%, and Q2 free cash flow was $227m, supporting strong but not exceptional momentum.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At $195.19, about $34.13b market cap, 125.73x trailing P/E and 50.66x forward P/E, valuation is demanding relative to roughly 10-11% FY27 revenue growth guidance.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 execution, cRPO conversion and emerging AI-agent identity adoption are identifiable catalysts, but monetization and share outcomes remain uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Founder-led continuity and improving profitability are constructive, while historical trust/security exposure and competitive execution requirements keep evidence in the adequate-to-strong range.

alignment2036.basis: Human and non-human identities require authentication, authorization and governance as cloud and AI-agent deployment expands, making identity infrastructure a durable strategic need.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Workforce Identity, Customer Identity, governance and emerging agent identity reuse a common identity-control capability across multiple demand surfaces.

bottleneckControl.basis: Identity/authentication is a required control point for digital access and Okta has substantial contracted demand, though competing identity stacks prevent unique bottleneck status.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Identity demand persists across cloud and AI scenarios, but customer consolidation into bundled platforms and security incidents can shift vendor economics.

substitutionResilience.basis: Identity controls are difficult to eliminate, but Okta-specific functionality can be substituted by Microsoft and other integrated security/identity platforms.

supplyChainResilience.basis: The subscription-software model has little direct physical input dependence; cash resources and partner/cloud architecture support operational resilience, while third-party infrastructure remains a dependency.

pricingPower.basis: Subscription economics, 13% GAAP operating margin and 28% FCF margin show value capture, but bundled competition limits evidence for durable exceptional pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks are demanding valuation, security/trust failure, bundled competition, AI-agent monetization uncertainty and slowing top-line growth; none is currently a gating contradiction.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability, operating results and balance-sheet facts are primary-source supported and valuation is current and independently sourced; confidence is reduced for future AI-agent economics and competitive share.

scoreRecord.thesis: Okta occupies a durable identity-control layer with improving profitability and contracted demand, while suite competition, trust sensitivity and a demanding valuation cap conviction.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A security/trust failure or successful bundled competitive response weakens retention and pricing while the current valuation leaves limited room for execution disappointment.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 FY2027 results and evidence that cRPO acceleration and AI-agent identity products convert into sustained revenue and cash-flow growth.

scoreBreakdown.note: Methodology 1.0 weighted component score; risk and confidence remain separate for downstream gate/penalty treatment.
